content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the go-to approach for building AI systems that answer questions using external documents. The standard recipe is well-known: chunk your documents, embed them into vectors, store them in a vector database, and perform similarity search at query time. But what if the retrieval step didn’t need any of that? A new approach called Vectorless RAG — pioneered by the PageIndex framework from VectifyAI — is challenging the assumption that vectors are essential for retrieval. It achieved 98.7% accuracy on the FinanceBench benchmark, significantly outperforming traditional vector-based RAG systems. That number alone makes it worth understanding.The Problem with Traditional RAGIn a typical RAG pipeline:Documents are split into fixed-size chunks (often by token count).

# Angular User Login UI
1. Create a new Angular project (Angular CLI required):
```bash
ng new library-frontend --routing --style=css
cd library-frontend
Copy the files from this document into your project's src/app and src/environments.
Update environment.apiBaseUrl if your backend URL changes.
Install dependencies (if needed):
npminstall
ngserve
Open http://localhost:4200 in your browser . Use credentials stored in your backend to sign
in.
Notes:  -  The  app  stores  access_token in  localStorage and  attaches  it  as
Authorization:  Bearer  <token>.  -  Adjust  token  expiration  checks  or  decode  the  JWT  in
AuthService if you want to validate expiration client-side before calling protected routes. ```
Final notes
This UI expects the backend to return a JSON with access_token and token_type (exactly as
your FastAPI authenticate_user returns {"access_token": ..., "token_type": 
"bearer"}).
